clue.text: People crying out for visitors?

definitions.meaning: those who shout or call aloud
people who call round at a house

explanation.surface: A question about whether those who shout are guests.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who calls out is a caller, and so is someone paying a visit at your house.

clue.text: Sweet coach arranged meal

parts.note: a railway coach is a car

indicators.note: the meal's letters are put in a new order

explanation.surface: A coach company has laid on a pudding.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sweet' looks like an adjective for the coach, but it is the definition, a noun. 'arranged' signals the anagram of the meal.
explanation.definitionFit: Caramel is a chewy toffee-like confection, a type of sweet.

clue.text: MP bas last missing man released

indicators.note: the last letter is gone from the word for an MP

parts.note: a Liberal is a member of parliament for the Liberal party
Ted is a man's name

explanation.surface: A politician whose last man is lost lets him go.
explanation.walkthrough: 'last missing' cuts the final L off LIBERAL; then add TED.
explanation.definitionFit: Liberated means freed, set loose from restraint.

clue.text: Put away in neat envelopes

indicators.note: the answer sits within the following words

explanation.surface: Something is stored in tidy envelopes.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer runs across 'neaT ENvelopes', starting inside 'neat'. 'Put away' is used here in its sense of consuming food.
explanation.definitionFit: Put away can mean eaten up, as in consuming a meal heartily.

clue.text: Insist upon its reversing back up behind

indicators.note: the little word runs backwards
this word is read in reverse order

parts.note: late means behind time

explanation.surface: Someone demands that it reverse, running behind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reversing' gives STI, 'back' turns UP to PU, then LATE.
explanation.definitionFit: To stipulate is to demand something as a condition, to insist upon it.

clue.text: Girl, encloses cheese for him

indicators.note: the girl wraps around the cheese, so one word sits inside the other

parts.note: gal is an informal word for a girl
Brie is a soft French cheese

explanation.surface: A young woman wraps up some cheese as a gift for a man.
explanation.walkthrough: 'him' is the definition: a man's name, the male form of Gabrielle. The cheese goes in after the girl's first two letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Gabriel is a male first name, so it can stand for a man referred to as him.

clue.text: Passes Georgia with backing group

parts.note: GA is the postal abbreviation for the US state of Georgia

indicators.note: the group's word runs backwards, from bottom up in this down clue

parts.note: set means group

explanation.surface: A singer from Georgia moves on with a backing group.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Passes' is a noun: a gate can be a narrow pass through mountains. 'backing' turns the group word upward in this down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: A gate is a mountain pass or narrow gap through which one may go.

clue.text: Grumble when standing on ale spilt here

indicators.note: in a down clue, standing puts the word upright, read bottom to top

parts.note: to crab is to complain

indicators.note: the letters are spilled out in a new order

explanation.surface: Someone complains while standing in a puddle of spilt beer at a bar.
explanation.walkthrough: 'standing' turns CRAB upward to BARC; 'spilt' rearranges ON and ALE to ELONA. 'here' points at the place the surface paints, a Barcelona bar.
explanation.definitionFit: The clue sets its scene in a city where beer is spilt, which here is the Catalan capital.

clue.text: Spotting, not overlooking, a sugary mixture

indicators.note: the word not is overlooked, meaning left out

parts.note: spotting is noticing
taken as written

explanation.surface: Seeing a sweet blend but not missing it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not, overlooking' means leave NOT out of NOTICING.
explanation.definitionFit: Icing is a sweet coating of sugar mixed with water or butter, spread on cakes.

clue.text: Still carrying overdue baby's outfit

indicators.note: the overdue word holds the still word inside it

parts.note: late means overdue
yet means still, as in not yet

explanation.surface: A mother still pregnant with an overdue baby buys its clothes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Still' is not a verb or adjective here but the adverb, as in 'not yet'; 'carrying' signals the container.
explanation.definitionFit: A layette is a full set of clothes and bedding for a newborn.

clue.text: Android's nonsense about black hole

indicators.note: the nonsense goes around the other pieces, enclosing them

parts.note: rot is a word for rubbish talk
B is the standard abbreviation for black, as on pencils
the letter O is round like a hole

explanation.surface: Someone dismisses an Android phone's talk of black holes as rubbish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts B and O inside ROT; the 's after 'Android' is 'is', a link.
explanation.definitionFit: An android is a machine built to look and act human, a kind of automaton.

clue.text: For nearly 3 months soccer side train

indicators.note: the season's name is not given complete, so a letter of it is lost

parts.note: winter is a season, three months long
City is a football team name, as in Manchester City

explanation.surface: A football team spends almost a whole season travelling by rail.
explanation.walkthrough: 'nearly' takes the W off WINTER here, from the front rather than the usual back. INTER is also a famous soccer side (Inter Milan).
explanation.definitionFit: An InterCity is a fast long-distance British rail service between major towns.

clue.text: Made me telephone Sue about cakes

parts.note: to ring is to phone someone

indicators.note: the letters are turned about, mixed into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone got a phone call from Sue about some baked treats.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' rearranges ME, RING and SUE into the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Meringues are light baked confections of whisked egg white and sugar, small sweet cakes.

clue.text: Crew ate noisily

indicators.note: the word is to be heard rather than read, giving a sound-alike

parts.note: past tense of eat, said the same as the number after seven

explanation.surface: A team dined loudly.
explanation.walkthrough: A rowing crew is called an eight, after its eight oarsmen.
explanation.definitionFit: In rowing, an eight is a boat crew of eight oarsmen and a cox.

clue.text: Delayed Installing hot machine

indicators.note: the delayed word has the hot letter set up inside it

parts.note: late means delayed or behind time
H is the abbreviation for hot, as on taps

explanation.surface: A heated machine was put in late.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Installing' puts H inside LATE.
explanation.definitionFit: A lathe is a workshop tool that spins a piece while it is shaped.

clue.text: A person he trained to make cans

indicators.note: the words are drilled into a new order

explanation.surface: A man was trained to make tins in a factory.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cans' is slang for headphones, not tins. 'trained' rearranges A PERSON HE.
explanation.definitionFit: Cans is slang for headphones, worn over the ears to listen.

clue.text: Alaskan city where hermits live?

definitions.meaning: an anchorite (hermit) dwells in an ..., the cell of a recluse

explanation.surface: A question about where recluses make their home in Alaska.
explanation.definitionFit: Anchorage is Alaska's biggest city; an anchorite is a religious recluse, and his cell is also an anchorage.

clue.text: Catch removing key from lorry needing cleansing

indicators.note: the key is taken away from the catch

parts.note: C is a musical key
an artic is an articulated lorry

explanation.surface: Someone catches a key off a lorry that needs a wash.
explanation.walkthrough: 'removing' drops one C from CATCH, leaving CATH; then ARTIC, British short for an articulated lorry.
explanation.definitionFit: Cathartic means purging or purifying, bringing a cleansing release.

clue.text: Cosmonaut ran out and sat shaking

indicators.note: the letters are shaken up and reordered

explanation.surface: A Russian space traveller ran out and sat down trembling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shaking' rearranges RAN OUT and SAT; 'and' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A cosmonaut is a Russian space traveller, the counterpart of an astronaut.

clue.text: We turned somersaults round pole, being experienced

indicators.note: the jumbled letters are wrapped around the pole
the words tumble over, so their letters are reordered

parts.note: N stands for the north pole

explanation.surface: Acrobats turned somersaults around a pole, as seasoned performers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'somersaults' rearranges WE TURNED to UDERWENT, and 'round' puts N inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Past tense of undergo: to have gone through something is to have experienced it.

clue.text: Puts drunk on craft of arrogant person

indicators.note: the letters are tipsy and reeling into a new order

parts.note: art means craft or skill

explanation.surface: A man tipsy on handicraft gets above himself.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drunk' rearranges PUTS to UPST; in a down clue 'on' puts it above ART.
explanation.definitionFit: An upstart is a self-important person who has risen suddenly and acts presumptuously.

clue.text: Current rubbish rejected by entertainer

parts.note: AC is alternating current

indicators.note: the rubbish is sent back, so read it backwards

parts.note: rot means rubbish

explanation.surface: A performer throws out a heap of present-day trash.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Current' looks like an adjective meaning present-day, but it is electrical current; 'rejected' turns the rubbish backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: An actor is a stage or screen performer, one kind of entertainer.

clue.text: Turned and went off holding article

indicators.note: the word for went off holds the article inside it

parts.note: rotted means went bad
a is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: Something spun round and then spoiled, keeping an object inside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'holding' puts A inside ROTTED.
explanation.definitionFit: Rotated means spun or revolved about an axis.

clue.text: Point out mum, embracing

indicators.note: the word for mum hugs the other word inside it

parts.note: mum means silent, and sh is a call for silence
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone shows their mother, giving her a hug.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mum' here means quiet ('keep mum'), not mother; 'embracing' signals that the call for hush holds the other word.
explanation.definitionFit: South is one of the four cardinal points of the compass.

clue.text: BBC head goes free

indicators.note: the first letter of the word is lost

parts.note: Auntie is a nickname for the BBC

explanation.surface: The head of the BBC is released.
explanation.walkthrough: The BBC is nicknamed 'Auntie' in Britain; 'head goes' removes its A.
explanation.definitionFit: To untie is to free something by undoing its knots.

clue.text: Got a space prepared for whipping boy

indicators.note: the letters are made ready in a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Someone cleared room for a boy who was to be punished.
explanation.walkthrough: 'prepared' rearranges GOT A SPACE.
explanation.definitionFit: A whipping boy takes the blame for others, just as a scapegoat does.

clue.text: Spot a way in outside

indicators.note: the way and in go outside the a, around it

parts.note: ST is short for street, a way
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone notices a path into the outside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'outside' tells the solver that the way and the in, side by side, sit around the single letter a.
explanation.definitionFit: A stain is a mark or blemish on a surface, a spot.

clue.text: Make happy Lawrence drink up first

indicators.note: the reversed drink comes before Lawrence
in a down clue the drink is read upward, in reverse

parts.note: ale is a beer
T. E. Lawrence, Lawrence of Arabia

explanation.surface: Lawrence is cheered up by having a drink first.
explanation.walkthrough: Lawrence is T. E. Lawrence, Lawrence of Arabia, known by his initials. 'up' reverses the drink in this down clue; 'first' puts it ahead.
explanation.definitionFit: To elate is to fill with joy, lifting someone's spirits.

clue.text: At holiday home Dan introduced servant

indicators.note: Dan is brought into the holiday home, placed inside it

parts.note: a tent is a camper's home on holiday
taken as written

explanation.surface: Dan was introduced to a servant at a holiday house.
explanation.walkthrough: A tent serves as a holiday home for campers; 'introduced' brings Dan inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: An attendant waits upon someone, a helper or servant.

clue.text: Expect delay after mid-day

indicators.note: the delay is placed after the middle letter
only the centre letter of the day is taken

parts.note: to wait is to hold back or delay

explanation.surface: A forecast of a hold-up in the afternoon.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mid' takes A, the middle of DAY; 'after' puts WAIT behind it.
explanation.definitionFit: To await something is to wait for it, anticipating it.

clue.text: Man not the cause of treachery

indicators.note: the man is excluded, so his letters are removed

parts.note: the reason is the cause of something
he is a pronoun for a man

explanation.surface: A man is not the source of the betrayal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not' removes HE from THE REASON, leaving T and REASON.
explanation.definitionFit: Treason is betrayal of one's country, the gravest form of treachery.

clue.text: Many less burnt made a fuss

indicators.note: less means minus, taking the letter away

parts.note: cremated means burnt to ashes
M is the Roman numeral 1000, so it stands for many

explanation.surface: Many fewer people made a scene about something burnt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'less' removes M from CREMATED. 'Create' is informal British for making a fuss.
explanation.definitionFit: In British slang, to create is to kick up a fuss or complain loudly.
